title: `podman machine info` - `machinestate` empty since 6.2.0
body:
### Issue Description We are using `podman machine info` to issue a `podman machine start` automatically if the `machinestate` is != running. Since podman 6.2.0 the `machinestate` is a empty string. We are using windows 11 with the WSL provider. ### Steps to reproduce the issue Steps to reproduce the issue - Windows side 1. `podman machine init --rootful --import-native-ca --playbook ` please note our network uses corporate proxies - the ENV-Variables are set while `podman machine init`
the corporate playbook sets e.g. the http/https/no_proxy for systemd & /etc/environment 3. `podman machine start` 4. `podman machine info` - `machinestate` is empty 5. `podman run busybox` succeeds comments.body: I checked a bit further - it looks to me that **with** (podman machine init) `--rootfull` the `machinetate`, `currentmachine` & `defaultmachine` field is empty.

I managed to debug using delve. The problem is a bit more puzzled.
One problem is that within the shells we have a network drive set (don't ask why) this one is reported by every WSL invocation with `wsl: Failed to translate '<driveLetter>:\\<path>'` . The check in
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/v6.2.0/pkg/machine/wsl/machine.go#L533-549
expects a bare `running` or `degraded` and thus fails.

The full content of `state` on my side is `wsl: Failed to translate '<driveLetter>:\\<path>'\nwsl: Failed to translate '<driveLetter>:\\<path>'\nrunning`.

Sorry for the confusion - but sometimes I execute scripts that that remove thos PATH components.

If the output is on stdout and the errors stderr then yes I Agree we should just parse stdout.
cc @l0rd

I can confirm that using 
```diff
- 	out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
+ 	out, err := cmd.Output()
```
is enough on my side. I am not a `sh` expert if a `.profile` may mix in some output as well.
@userid0x0, thank you. Can you try to run `wsl -u root -d podman-default-machine sh systemctl is-system-running`?

@l0rd not a big deal
```
wsl: Failed to translate '<driveLetter>:\\<path>'
wsl: Failed to translate '<driveLetter2>:\\<path2>'
running
```

@userid0x0 thank you. And your fix looks perfect 👍 I will open a PR. In the meantime, if you have the chance, can you try to append

```conf
[interop]
appendWindowsPath=false
```

to the file `/etc/wsl.conf`, inside the `podman-machine-default` wsl instance, and see if that changes something (i.e. it solves the `machinestate` problem)?
